$comment: Rule catalog — data. Standards 3, 4, 17. Provenance, versioning, and lineage: the three records that make it possible to say what a model was trained on and whether a feature could legitimately have been used. Two entries carry detectors, and both detect the absence of a document rather than the truth of one.

rules.title: Dataset provenance is recorded and discoverable
rules.description: Every dataset has a written record of where it came from, when it was obtained, what population or process it represents, what each row is, and what was excluded from it — discoverable from the dataset rather than only from the memory of whoever built it.
rules.rationale: A dataset is a claim about the world, and the claim cannot be assessed without knowing how it was obtained and what was left out. Exclusions matter most and are recorded least: dropping rows with missing values does not remove noise, it removes the population for whom that field is missing.
rules.remediation: Add a dataset card — DATASET.md or DATA_CARD.md — covering origin, collection mechanism, population, unit of observation, and an exclusions section listing each rule applied with the count and proportion it removed.
rules.evidenceExpected: A provenance document carrying origin, collection, population, and exclusions sections, plus an attestation that the exclusions listed are all of them.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes that a provenance document exists and carries the expected sections. It cannot establish that the content is accurate, current, or complete, and it can never detect an exclusion that was applied and not written down — the evidence of the removal is precisely what was removed.

rules.title: Observations are not removed to improve a metric
rules.description: Observations must not be removed because of what their removal does to a reported number. The prohibited act is the combination: removal, driven by the metric, undisclosed.
rules.rationale: Removing hard cases raises every score while removing exactly the population the model most needs to handle. The resulting figure describes performance on a problem nobody has.
rules.remediation: Restore the excluded observations and re-evaluate, or justify the exclusion by a rule that was specified before the results were seen and record it with its effect.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation that each exclusion was rule-driven and pre-specified rather than selected after a disappointing evaluation, with the provenance document's exclusions section as supporting evidence.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. An exclusion applied before results were seen and one applied after them are byte-identical in the code that performs them; the difference is intent and sequence, neither of which is in the repository.

rules.title: Datasets carry an identifier that changes with their contents
rules.description: Each dataset carries an identifier — a version, a content hash, a manifest of files and checksums, or a data-versioning tool's revision — that differs whenever the contents differ. A filename is not an identifier.
rules.rationale: A dataset that can change while its name stays the same makes every past result unverifiable and every comparison unsound: two models said to have been evaluated on the same data may not have been, and nothing records which.
rules.remediation: Add a versioning mechanism beside the data — a .dvc file, a lockfile, a manifest, or adjacent checksums — and cite the identifier from the experiment records that used it.
rules.evidenceExpected: A version manifest, lockfile, or checksum set covering the datasets in use, and experiment records naming the version each result came from.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check establishes that data exists and that no pinning mechanism was found beside it. Its silence establishes only that a mechanism exists — not that the identifier changes when the contents do, not that the training run used the version the manifest names, and not that any result cited it.

rules.title: Each feature's sources, transformation, and availability time are recorded
rules.description: For every feature, a record names the raw sources it derives from, the transformation that produced it, and when its underlying data becomes available relative to the prediction moment.
rules.rationale: Lineage exists to make two other reviews possible: whether a feature will exist at inference, and whether it encodes the target. Both are properties of where a value comes from and when — never of the value itself — so without the record, neither question can be answered reliably.
rules.remediation: Build a feature register, documented schema, or feature-store definition naming sources, transformations, and availability timing per feature, and keep it current with the transformation code.
rules.evidenceExpected: A lineage record sufficient to answer, for each feature, whether it derives from information unavailable at prediction time and whether it derives from the target.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. A scanner can see that a function consumes one column and produces another; it cannot see that the source column is populated by a nightly job that runs after the event being predicted. A name-and-dtype listing and a genuine lineage record are indistinguishable to a scan.

rules.title: The dataset's purpose, owner, size, sampling and suitability are recorded
rules.description: The dataset record states the purpose and task the dataset was created for, who created it and on whose behalf, the total number of instances for each task type, the sampling strategy if it is a sample of a larger set, why the set it was drawn from suits the task, and why the dataset is suitable for the modelling task at hand.
rules.rationale: A dataset assembled for one purpose and reused for another carries label and sampling choices that were reasonable for the first and unexamined for the second. Without the owner, the size and the sampling strategy, a reader cannot judge what the data can support or whom to ask.
rules.remediation: Extend the dataset card with purpose, creator and owning entity, instance counts per task type, the sampling strategy and the justification for the sampling frame, and a short statement of why the dataset suits the modelling task.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset card or provenance document stating purpose, creator, instance counts, sampling strategy, sampling-frame justification and task suitability.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement is accurate and sufficient is a judgement about prose, and a scan cannot make it.

rules.title: Missing information, errors, noise and redundancy are recorded with their rates
rules.description: The dataset record describes information missing from individual instances and why it is missing, states the percentage of missing data (split by class for a categorical outcome), and describes known errors, sources of noise and redundancies.
rules.rationale: Missingness and noise are properties of the data that no model-side check recovers. A model trained on data whose missing values are concentrated in one class learns that concentration as signal.
rules.remediation: Add to the dataset record the missing-data description and its cause, the percentage of missing data (split by class where the outcome is categorical), and the known errors, noise sources and redundancies.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record with the percentage of missing data (split by class where the outcome is categorical), the reason for missingness, and a list of known errors, noise and redundancy.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement is accurate and sufficient is a judgement about prose, and a scan cannot make it.

rules.title: The dataset record states what it must not be used for and what may affect future uses
rules.description: The dataset record states the tasks for which the dataset should not be used, and anything about its composition, collection, preprocessing, cleaning or labelling that might affect future uses.
rules.rationale: Conclusions drawn from a dataset are valid only for the uses its composition supports. A recorded boundary lets a later project check its use against it instead of rediscovering the limit through failure.
rules.remediation: Add an intended-use and out-of-scope-use section to the dataset record, including known collection and preprocessing effects on later use.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record section naming unsuitable tasks and known composition or preprocessing impacts on future uses.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement is accurate and sufficient is a judgement about prose, and a scan cannot make it.

rules.title: Distribution, licence and third-party restrictions are recorded
rules.description: The dataset record states whether the dataset is distributed to third parties outside the entity it was created for and on what permission basis, the copyright or other licence and terms of use it is distributed under, and any intellectual-property or other restrictions third parties have imposed on the data.
rules.rationale: Distribution, licence and third-party restrictions govern what a dataset may lawfully be used for, and a model trained on data used outside its terms inherits the breach. Recording them where the dataset is described makes the question answerable by someone who was not there.
rules.remediation: Add distribution, licence or terms of use, and third-party restrictions to the dataset record, or state that they are unknown.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record stating whether the data is distributed externally and on what basis, the licence or terms, and any third-party restrictions, or an explicit unknown.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement about licence, permission or sensitivity is true is a judgement about the data and its history, and a scan does not read either.

rules.title: Whether the data is confidential, identifies individuals or is sensitive is recorded, or recorded as unknown
rules.description: The dataset record states whether the data may be confidential or legally privileged, whether individuals can be identified from it directly or indirectly and on what basis, and whether it holds sensitive content, including personal data in training, validation and vocabulary files. Where this has not been assessed the record says unknown.
rules.rationale: A model trained on data whose sensitivity nobody assessed carries that sensitivity silently. Recording the status, or recording that it is unknown, separates not looked at from looked at and absent. No protected attribute needs to be collected to answer it.
rules.remediation: Add a sensitivity statement to the dataset record: confidential or privileged content, whether individuals are identifiable and how that was assessed, and sensitive content, each as yes, no with basis, or unknown.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record with a confidentiality, identifiability and sensitive-content statement for each dataset, each answered yes, no with basis, or unknown.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement about licence, permission or sensitivity is true is a judgement about the data and its history, and a scan does not read either.

rules.title: Known defects and the update policy of a dataset version are recorded
rules.description: The record of a dataset version states whether it has an erratum and where it is, and whether the dataset will be updated (to correct labelling errors, add or delete instances), how often, by whom, and how updates are communicated.
rules.rationale: A reused version is only the version that was evaluated if its defects and its update policy are known. A corrected label or a deleted instance changes what a result means, and without an erratum or an update policy a later reader cannot tell which version a result applies to.
rules.remediation: Record a link or access point for the erratum (or state there is none) and describe the update policy and how updates are communicated beside the version identifier.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record or manifest stating the erratum location or none, and the update frequency, owner and communication route.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement about a dataset's history is complete and true is a judgement about that history, which a scan does not read.

rules.title: Earlier uses of the dataset are recorded
rules.description: The dataset record states whether the dataset has already been used for any tasks and describes those uses, so that reuse of a held-out or test partition can be assessed.
rules.rationale: A dataset used for earlier tasks may already have been used to select, tune or evaluate models. Prior uses are evidence of test-set reuse and of leakage risk, and they are invisible unless someone wrote them down.
rules.remediation: Add a prior-uses section to the dataset record: tasks the dataset has been used for, by whom, and whether any partition was used for selection or tuning.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record listing prior uses and any prior selection or tuning on its partitions, or stating that there are none.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a written statement about a dataset's history is complete and true is a judgement about that history, which a scan does not read.

rules.title: Whether the dataset identifies subpopulations, and how, is recorded or recorded as unknown
rules.description: The dataset record states whether the dataset identifies any subpopulations, for example by age or gender, and if it does, how they are identified and what the distribution across them is. Where subpopulations are not identified, or where recording them would be unlawful or inappropriate, the record says so rather than leaving the question blank.
rules.rationale: Group-level analysis is only possible for groups the data can name, so what the dataset does and does not identify bounds what any later analysis can show. Recording it, including recording not identified or unknown, keeps a missing attribute from being read as an absence of the issue. No protected or sensitive attribute needs to be collected to answer it.
rules.remediation: Add a subpopulation statement to the dataset record: whether subpopulations are identified, by what method, and their distribution, or not identified, or unknown, with the reason.
rules.evidenceExpected: A dataset record with a subpopulation statement for each dataset: identified with method and distribution, not identified, or unknown, each with a reason.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Whether a stated identification method is accurate, and whether an attribute should be recorded at all, are judgements about the data and the law that a scan does not read.
